from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Complex periodic signals are just chords of sine waves.", "A cat’s purr reveals a base and harmonics.", "Chaotic waves resolve into ordered stacks of harmonics."]
        self.setup_layout("The Hook: The Musical Analogy", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define animated objects
        staff = VGroup(*[Line(LEFT*2, RIGHT*2) for _ in range(5)]).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
        notes = VGroup(*[Dot(color=WHITE) for _ in range(10)])
        
        melody_line = VGroup(*[Dot(color=YELLOW) for _ in range(5)])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display a musical staff with scattered notes appearing. (Color: #FFFFFF)
        self.place_at_grid(staff, 'B2', scale_factor=0.6)
        for i, note in enumerate(notes):
            self.place_at_grid(note, f"{chr(ord('A')+i//6)}{1+i%6}")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(staff), *[FadeIn(note) for note in notes])
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate notes coalescing into a single clear melody line. (Color: #FFFF00)
        self.play(
            *[FadeOut(note) for note in notes],
            FadeIn(melody_line)
        )
        for i, note in enumerate(melody_line):
            self.place_at_grid(note, f"C{i+1}")
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight the melody line with a vibrant pulse. (Color: #00FFFF)
        self.play(Indicate(melody_line, color="#00FFFF"))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Periodic f(x) decomposes into sums of sines and cosines.",
            "Fourier coefficients represent the weight of each frequency.",
            "Think of it like a harmonic light mixer."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Core Concept: Defining Fourier Series", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # Draw a periodic square wave
        square_wave = Axes(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1], y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1],
            x_length=5, y_length=3, axis_config={"include_numbers": False}
        )
        def square_func(x):
            return 1 if np.sin(x) >= 0 else -1
        
        graph_square = square_wave.plot(square_func, color="#FFFFFF", discontinuities=[0, np.pi, -np.pi])
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(square_wave, graph_square), "C3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(graph_square))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")
        
        # Show a single sine wave overlapping the square wave
        sine_wave = square_wave.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x), color="#FF00FF")
        self.play(Create(sine_wave))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        # Add more sine waves (harmonic 3) to approximate the square
        sine_wave_3 = square_wave.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x) + (1/3)*np.sin(3*x), color="#00FF00")
        self.play(Transform(sine_wave, sine_wave_3))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Orthogonality allows us to sift specific frequency components.",
            "Integration acts as a tuner for frequencies.",
            "This isolates pure signals from the static air."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing Coefficients: The Integration Trick", lecture_lines)
        
        # Formula: a_n = \frac{1}{\pi} \int_{-\pi}^{\pi} f(x) \cos(nx) dx
        formula = MathTex(
            "a_n = ", "\\frac{1}{\pi}", "\\int_{-\\pi}^{\\pi}", "f(x)", "\\cos(nx)", "dx"
        ).set_color(WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B3", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        # Orthogonality/Integration highlight
        integral_part = formula[2]
        ortho_box = SurroundingRectangle(integral_part, color=RED, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(ortho_box))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Show signal separation concept
        sine_wave = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(4 * x), x_range=[-PI, PI], color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(sine_wave, "E3", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Create(sine_wave))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Summing harmonics builds complex waves piece by piece.",
            "Adding more terms reveals sharp square wave edges.",
            "Gibbs phenomenon appears at the sharp corners."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Step-by-Step Construction: Synthesis", lecture_lines)
        self.lecture.set_opacity(0)
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3, 1], y_range=[-2, 2, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.add(axes)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")))
        base_line = Line(axes.c2p(-3, 0), axes.c2p(3, 0), color="#FFFFFF")
        self.play(Create(base_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")))
        
        fund = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x * np.pi), color="#FFFF00")
        self.play(Create(fund))
        
        # Second harmonic
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")))
        harm2 = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x * np.pi) + (1/3)*np.sin(3 * x * np.pi), color="#00FFFF")
        self.play(Transform(fund, harm2))
        
        # Final convergence representation
        final_sum = axes.plot(lambda x: sum((4/np.pi) * (np.sin((2*n-1)*x*np.pi)/(2*n-1)) for n in range(1, 10)), color="#00FF00")
        self.play(Transform(fund, final_sum), run_time=2)
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "We map signals from time into frequency domains.",
            "Noise-canceling headphones neutralize drone frequencies instantly.",
            "Fourier analysis transforms our digital, modern world."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion & Application", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display real-world signal processing icons. (Color: #FFFFFF)
        icon_time = VGroup(
            Line(LEFT, RIGHT),
            *[Dot(np.array([x, np.sin(x*3)*0.5, 0])) for x in np.linspace(-1, 1, 10)]
        ).set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(icon_time, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(icon_time))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show signal decomposition into frequency components. (Color: #00FFFF)
        decomp = VGroup(
            Line(ORIGIN, UP*1.5),
            Line(ORIGIN, RIGHT*1.5)
        ).set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(decomp, 'B5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(decomp))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Emphasize final spectrum output with a bar graph. (Color: #FFFF00)
        bars = VGroup(*[Rectangle(height=np.random.rand()*1.5, width=0.2, color="#FFFF00", fill_opacity=1) for _ in range(5)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(bars, 'D3', 'F5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(bars))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Pure Fourier Series: Decoding the Language of Waves

sections.title: The Hook: The Musical Analogy
sections.content: Introduce the concept that any complex periodic signal is just a chord made of pure notes. Prerequisites: Familiarity with basic trigonometry (sine and cosine waves). Visual: A chaotic wave flattening into a layered stack of simple, smooth sine waves.
sections.example: A smart cat's purr: Analyzing how the complex rumble is actually a combination of a fundamental 'base' frequency and higher-pitched harmonics.

sections.title: The Core Concept: Defining Fourier Series
sections.content: Define the Fourier Series as a decomposition of a periodic function f(x) into an infinite sum of sines and cosines. Emphasize that the coefficients (a_n, b_n) represent the 'weight' or intensity of each frequency component.
sections.example: A light-mixing console where each slider (harmonic) changes the shape of the output wave.

sections.title: Visualizing Coefficients: The Integration Trick
sections.content: Explain the orthogonality of sines and cosines. Use the 'Inner Product' concept to show how we 'sift' out specific frequencies. Visual: An animation of a filter sliding over a wave, isolating one specific sine component.
sections.example: A radio tuner: Turning the knob (calculating the coefficient) to isolate a specific signal from the static of the airwaves.

sections.title: Step-by-Step Construction: Synthesis
sections.content: Show the additive process. Starting with the fundamental frequency (n=1), add n=2, n=3... up to n=infinity. Visual: A square wave emerging as we sum more sine terms, showing the 'Gibbs phenomenon' at sharp edges.
sections.example: A 3D printer nozzle tracing a square path; the motors combine simple back-and-forth movements to create a rigid, sharp-cornered shape.

sections.title: Conclusion & Application
sections.content: Summarize the transformation from Time Domain to Frequency Domain. Connect this to modern technology. Visual: A split screen showing a heartbeat signal (time) vs. its clean pulse spectrum (frequency).
sections.example: Noise-canceling headphones: A device that uses Fourier analysis to detect background drone frequencies and injects the 'negative' phase to neutralize them instantly.
